content.overview: BNS s. 346 — Tampering with property mark with intent to cause injury.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Tampering with property mark with intent to cause injury. BNS restatement of IPC 480 / 489. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 480 / 489. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 346 is the rule on “Tampering with property mark with intent to cause injury”. The section provides that whoever removes, destroys, defaces or adds to any property mark, intending or knowing it to be likely that he may thereby cause injury to any person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 346 exists so that “Tampering with property mark with intent to cause injury” has a closed legal test in Chapter XVIII — Of Offences Relating to Documents and to Property Marks. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: False documents, forgery, using a forged electronic record, property marks.

The provision in detail
346. Whoever removes, destroys, defaces or adds to any property mark, intending or knowing it to be likely that he may thereby cause injury to any person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both
